title: KDP or IngramSpark Won't Take Your JPG or PNG Cover? How to Make a Print PDF | SparkPrep
h1: How to fix a book cover saved as a JPG or PNG instead of a PDF
description: Paperback covers must be uploaded as a PDF. Learn why a JPG or PNG cover is turned away and how to turn it into a print-ready PDF.
lead: Your cover looks perfect as a picture. But for a printed book, KDP and IngramSpark want a PDF.
error: Cover file must be a PDF
errorNote: Paraphrased. Each printer words this a little differently.
why:
A JPG or PNG is just a picture. A print cover file also has to carry its exact size in inches, bleed and print color. That's why paperback cover uploads at KDP and IngramSpark expect a PDF.

Picture files bring other problems too: PNG and most JPGs are in screen color (RGB), and a picture saved for the web is usually far below 300 DPI at full cover size.
manual: Check your picture is at least 300 DPI at the full cover size (width in inches x 300 = pixels needed).
Open it in a design app and make a document at your printer's exact full cover size, including bleed.
Place the picture so it fills the whole page edge to edge.
Export as a PDF, using PDF/X-1a:2001 and CMYK if your app offers them.
Re-upload it to your printer and wait for the file review again. If it fails, you start over.
quickfix: Upload your JPG, PNG or TIFF cover. SparkPrep checks its size and resolution, converts it to print color, and exports a print-ready PDF/X-1a.

cta.text: Upload your cover as a JPG, PNG or TIFF. SparkPrep checks the size and DPI, converts it to CMYK and exports a PDF/X-1a your printer accepts.
cta.button: Turn my cover into a PDF

faq.q: Can I upload a JPG cover to KDP for a paperback?
faq.a: No. KDP's paperback cover upload expects a PDF. Turn the picture into a PDF at the exact full cover size first.

faq.q: Does saving a JPG as a PDF fix it?
faq.a: Only if the PDF is the exact full cover size with bleed, and the picture has enough resolution at that size.
